arxiv-2305-13983.title: Regimes of electronic transport in doped InAs nanowire.
arxiv-2305-13983.creator: A A Zhukov, I E Batov
arxiv-2305-13983.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by A A Zhukov, I E Batov. We report on the low temperature measurements of the magnetotransport in Si-doped InAs quantum wire in the presence of a charged tip of an atomic force microscope serving as a mobile gate, i.e. scanning gate microscopy (SGM). By altering the carrier concentration with back gate voltage, we transfer the wire through several transport regimes: from residual Coulomb blockade to nonlinear resonance regime, followed by linear resonance regime and, finally, to almost homogeneous diffusion regime.

arxiv-2404-14283.description: Abstract Chromatic break and/or plateau observed in the early optical and X-ray afterglow lightcurves challenge the conventional external shock models of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Detection of TeV gamma-ray afterglows indicates strong gamma-ray production within the afterglow jets. We investigate the cascade radiations of the e ± e^{\pm} production via the γ ​ γ \gamma\gamma interaction in the jets.

arxiv-2505-06749.description: Abstract As transportation technology advances, the demand for connected vehicle infrastructure has greatly increased to improve their efficiency and safety. arxiv-2508-03747.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Mobility Periodicity for Understanding Urban Transportation Systems
arxiv-2508-03747.creator: Xinyu Chen, Qi Wang, Yunhan Zheng, Nina Cao, HanQin Cai, Jinhua Zhao
arxiv-2508-03747.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xinyu Chen, Qi Wang, Yunhan Zheng, Nina Cao, HanQin Cai, Jinhua Zhao. Uncovering the temporal regularity of human mobility is crucial for discovering urban dynamics and has implications for various decision-making processes and urban system applications. This study formulates the periodicity quantification problem in complex and multidimensional human mobility data as a sparse identification of dominant positive auto-correlations in time series autoregression, allowing one to discover and quantify significant periodic patterns such as weekly periodicity from a data-driven and interpretable machine learning perspective.

pmc-10537603.creator: Jiaxiang Jiang, Michael Goebel, Cezar Borba, William Smith, B S Manjunath
pmc-10537603.description: We consider the problem of finding an accurate representation of neuron shapes, extracting sub-cellular features, and classifying neurons based on neuron shapes. In neuroscience research, the skeleton representation is often used as a compact and abstract representation of neuron shapes. However, existing methods are limited to getting and analyzing “curve” skeletons which can only be applied for tubular shapes.

pmc-10565222.title: Dual diagnosis of TBI and SCI: an epidemiological study in the pediatric population
pmc-10565222.creator: Joslyn Gober, Lauren T. Shapiro, Eduard Tiozzo, Nanichi A. Ramos Roldán, Cristina M. Brea, Katherine Lin, Adriana Valbuena
pmc-10565222.description: IntroductionDual diagnosis (DD) with traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) poses clinical and rehabilitation challenges. While comorbid TBI is common among adults with SCI, little is known about the epidemiology in the pediatric population. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of TBI among children in the United States hospitalized with SCI.

pmc-11497434.creator: Flor Castro-Rodriguez, Yakdiel Rodriguez-Gallo
pmc-11497434.description: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare lung disease that primarily affects women. A patient with a medical history of Tuberous Sclerosis-Associated Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (TSC-LAM), a prior thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer, chronic hypertension, and a previous pulmonary thromboembolism was admitted to the hospital. Following the stabilization of her clinical condition, diaphragmatic exercises and incentive spirometers were implemented.

pmc-13178568.creator: E Liu, Xijia Xin, Mengdong Shi, Weikai Han, Qingyu Ren, Yaqi Tang, Yanan Yue, Chenyu Zhang, Zhanpeng Gao, Qingwei Yue, Jinhao Sun

This study reveals a circuit through which Fos-positive neurons in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN) regulate gastritis via a PVN–dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus–stomach neural circuit and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis.

pmc-13306163.description: Objectives: The study aimed to investigate the antibacterial, in vitro anti-inflammatory and anti-acne properties of Patchouli essential oil (PEO). The antibacterial activity of PEO against Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes) and Staphylococcus epidermidis (S. epidermidis) was evaluated via MIC detection and growth curve analysis.

pmc-13385056.title: The Queen Square cognitive assessment screen (Q-CAS): normative data and validation in acute stroke
pmc-13385056.creator: Edgar Chan, Maria del Rocio Hidalgo Mas, Adrian So, Robert Simister, David J. Werring, Parashkev Nachev, Lisa Cipolotti
pmc-13385056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAccurate and comprehensive assessment of cognition after stroke is crucial for diagnosis and rehabilitation. However, detailed assessment by a Neuropsychologist is often not feasible or practical. Although many screening tools exist, none fulfill three critical criteria: 1) assess all stroke-relevant domains, 2) consider demographic variables of gender, age, education level, and whether English is a first or second language, and 3) is brief and can be easily administered.MethodsThe Q-CAS was developed by adapting well-validated neuropsychological tests.

pmc-13407712.title: Acetabular cup orientation differs across surgical approaches in primary total hip arthroplasty: a retrospective analysis

pmc-13407712.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We hypothesized that acetabular cup orientation may differ according to the surgical approach used.

pmc-13628713.title: Psychosocial and cognitive profiles associated with health-related quality of life and healthy aging among community-dwelling older adults: a latent profile analysis
pmc-13628713.creator: Sunmin Lee, Youmin Cho, Rhayun Song
pmc-13628713.description: BackgroundCommunity-dwelling older adults differ in their social, psychological, and cognitive resources, which may influence health-related quality of life and healthy aging. Variable-centered approaches may not fully capture this heterogeneity. This study aimed to identify psychosocial and cognitive profiles among community-dwelling older adults and examine differences in health-related quality of life and healthy aging across profiles.
